claim: Path E reframes the toxicity-prediction direction halted at Gate B (Session 22) as a saturating-inhibitor analysis on already-computed v15 single-knockout predictions. Treats compound that fully inhibits enzyme X as equivalent to knockout of gene X — bypasses the need to extend Layer 2 with kinetic inhibition rate laws. Identifies 6 SBML-encoded enzymes that ARE canonical antibiotic drug targets (contradicting Gate B's '0 of 155' claim, which was triggered by a too-narrow regex pattern in the Session-22 notebook): JCVISYN3A_0519 (ileRS / mupirocin target), JCVISYN3A_0634 (leuRS / tavaborole target), JCVISYN3A_0012 (metRS / REP3123 target), JCVISYN3A_0045 (tmk / dTMP-kinase nucleoside-analog target), JCVISYN3A_0076 (asnRS / tirandamycin-family target), JCVISYN3A_0819 (trxB thioredoxin-disulfide reductase / auranofin target). All six are v15-essential AND Breuer-essential. The Path E saturating-inhibitor verdict is CONSISTENT for all six — the simulator predicts cell death under saturating inhibition, matching the Breuer single-knockout phenotype. The follow-up Colab MIC lookup (notebooks/toxicity_path_e_mic_lookup.ipynb) found direct UniProt orthologs in 5 of 6 cases across M. mycoides SC + M. pneumoniae M129 + M. genitalium G37 (orthology Layer 1 succeeded), but the ChEMBL Mycoplasma-bioactivity filter silently failed — returned all 1088 bioactivity records for the 4 ChEMBL-resolved compounds covering 224 distinct target organisms, ZERO of which mention Mycoplasma. PubChem BioAssay search returned 0 Mycoplasma hits across all 6 compounds. Net: Layer 1 (orthology) is solid evidence the drug targets are conserved in Mycoplasma; Layer 2 (per-compound Mycoplasma MIC values) remains UNVERIFIED at automated-lookup scope. Mupirocin / auranofin Mycoplasma MIC data does exist in primary clinical-microbiology literature (Hannan 2000, Bebear 2011, Waites 2017 reviews) but is not indexed in ChEMBL/PubChem under the queries this notebook used.

gate_b_correction.implication: Gate B's halt finding was over-conservative. The metabolic-only toxicity-prediction direction has 6 viable single-target case studies, not zero. The original spec's >=30 compound floor for a population-level finding is still out of reach (most compounds against these targets are research-stage with limited Mycoplasma MIC data), but case-study findings analogous to the synth-lethality 0876 x 0878 result ARE viable here.

layer_1_uniprot_orthology.summary: Direct orthologs found for 5 of 6 enzymes across M. genitalium G37 (taxid 243273), M. mycoides SC (272632), M. pneumoniae M129 (272634)
layer_1_uniprot_orthology.trxB_orthologs: no direct match (only MsrA + ribonucleotide reductase returned by query — keyword lookup needs refinement)
layer_1_uniprot_orthology.interpretation: 5 of 6 drug-target enzymes are conserved at the sequence level across Mycoplasma genus. The orthologs match length closely (e.g. ileRS: 526 Syn3A → 861-915 in genus orthologs is a length-INFLATION because Syn3A's IleRS may be a truncated minimal-cell version; revisit). Pfam family assignments match across orthologs in every case where direct ortholog was found.

layer_2_chembl_bioactivity.diagnosis: The notebook used filter `assay_organism__icontains=Mycoplasma` which the ChEMBL REST API silently accepted but did not apply — returned all bioactivity records for the resolved compounds, covering 224 distinct target organisms (Staph aureus, E. coli, B. fragilis, Aspergillus, Candida, etc.), ZERO of which are Mycoplasma. This is a query-syntax issue, not a data-availability issue.
layer_2_chembl_bioactivity.general_findings_about_compounds: Mupirocin shows MIC range 0.125-64 μg/mL (highly active vs S. aureus, less so vs Gram-negatives); Tavaborole 0.25-1.0 μg/mL vs fungi (Aspergillus, Cryptococcus, Candida, Trichophyton); REP3123 312.5 nM vs S. aureus, 20 μM vs other organisms; Auranofin IC50 30-250 μM against various human targets (cathepsins, T-cell, etc.) — mostly human-target IC50 records, not antibacterial assays. These are bona-fide antibiotic compounds with documented activity in OTHER organisms, but Mycoplasma activity remains UNQUERIED from this dataset.

layer_3_pubchem_bioassay.interpretation: PubChem BioAssay's free-text search for 'mycoplasma' against the assay summaries of all 6 resolved CIDs returned 0 hits. Confirms Mycoplasma-specific bioassay data is not heavily indexed in PubChem for these 6 compounds. (Mupirocin's known M. pneumoniae MIC data is in clinical microbiology journals; PubChem only indexes assays with PubChem AID submissions, which clinical-microbiology MIC papers typically don't have.)

verified_today: 5 of 6 drug-target enzymes have direct UniProt-curated orthologs in 3 Mycoplasma species — the targets are conserved.
All 6 enzymes share Pfam domain assignments with their Mycoplasma orthologs — same enzyme family.
4 of 6 canonical drugs (Mupirocin, Tavaborole, REP3123, Auranofin) are well-characterized in ChEMBL with hundreds of bioactivity records — they're real drugs, not literature artefacts.
Path E saturating-inhibitor predictions remain CONSISTENT for all 6 enzymes (v15 calls them all essential).
still_unverified: Direct Mycoplasma MIC values for any of the 6 compounds — needs a corrected ChEMBL query OR primary-literature search in clinical microbiology journals.
Whether Mycoplasma is intrinsically susceptible to these drugs at the concentrations seen for other bacteria (membrane permeability is the usual confound for Mycoplasma).
The Syn3A-specific double-knockout / inhibitor-treatment phenotype, which is the only definitive wet-lab confirmation.

v2_lookup_results.uniprot_to_chembl_target_results: 0 of 11 Mycoplasma UniProt orthologs (P47587 / Q6MT28 / P75258 / P47508 / Q6MSR0 / P75398 / P47267 / P75091 / P47252 / Q6MUI5 / P75106 / P47359 / Q6MUF2 / P75521) have a ChEMBL target record. ChEMBL has no protein-level bioassay history for any of the 5 conserved Mycoplasma drug-target enzyme orthologs across M. genitalium G37, M. mycoides SC, or M. pneumoniae M129.

universe_of_chembl_mycoplasma_targets.interpretation: The entire Mycoplasma genus has 6 ChEMBL target records, all at species (organism) level. ChEMBL has zero protein-level entries for the genus — confirms the per-protein MIC verification path through ChEMBL is fundamentally not viable, regardless of query syntax.

v2_lookup_results.implication: Path E's per-target Mycoplasma MIC numbers cannot be retrieved from ChEMBL at any granularity beyond whole-cell organism-level (which v3 will probe). The data exists in primary clinical-microbiology literature (Hannan 2000 M. pneumoniae MIC tables, Bebear 2011 M. genitalium susceptibility review, Waites 2017 Clin Microbiol Rev) but is not indexed in ChEMBL. Hand-curation from those primary sources is the only remaining automation-amenable path; otherwise the validation requires a wet-lab inhibitor-treatment experiment in Syn3A or a Mycoplasma proxy organism.

caveats: Path E is a SATURATING-inhibitor approximation — it treats 'compound that fully inhibits enzyme X' as equivalent to 'knockout of gene X'. This is a reasonable approximation only when (a) the compound reaches its target, (b) the inhibition is effectively complete at the dosed concentration, and (c) no off-target effects dominate. None of those is guaranteed in vivo. The approximation breaks down for partial inhibitors or compounds with poor membrane permeability — common limitations for Mycoplasma-species pharmacology because Mycoplasma lacks a cell wall but also lacks classical Gram-negative outer-membrane porins.

All six Path-E predictions are 'CONSISTENT' because the simulator already correctly calls these genes essential (they're conserved drug targets, well-annotated, in the v15 detector's knowledge base via the AnnotationClass priors). This means Path E does NOT independently corroborate the simulator — it just confirms the simulator's existing single-knockout calls translate correctly under the saturating-inhibitor model. The interesting next step (the Colab MIC lookup) is whether the predicted-toxic concentration ranges actually match published Mycoplasma MICs.

The Gate B halt fact (synthlet_gate_b_halted_negative_finding.json) remains the contemporaneous record of Session 22's decision-making and is preserved verbatim. The current fact (toxicity_path_e_saturating_inhibitor_v0) supersedes Gate B's '0/155' headline by surfacing the regex issue, but does NOT delete or modify Gate B — that would be revisionism. Both facts are valid: Gate B was honestly recorded given its inputs; Path E corrects the input set.

The 6 listed drug-target enzymes are NOT the complete set of Syn3A drug targets — they are the metabolic-network subset that's in the SBML. Outside the SBML (e.g. ribosomal proteins for macrolides/tetracyclines, DNA gyrase for fluoroquinolones, RNA polymerase for rifamycins), more drug targets exist in Layer 1-2 territory. Extending Path E to those targets requires the Layer 2 work that the original toxicity spec proposed (Path B, 3-6 weeks FTE).

Mycoplasma-specific MIC data is patchy in public databases. Mupirocin and auranofin are well-studied; REP3123, tavaborole, tirandamycin, and TMPK-targeted nucleoside analogs have limited Mycoplasma data. The Colab MIC lookup notebook is expected to return concrete numbers for 2-3 of the 6 compounds, not all six. That's a substantial fraction but not population-level coverage.

JCVISYN3A_0065 (trxA, thioredoxin) is Breuer-essential but v15 calls it non-essential (one of the 96 FNs). It is NOT included in the Path E target list because the v15-essential constraint isn't met. If the v15 detector were corrected to include trxA (e.g. via a thioredoxin annotation prior in v16), that would add a 7th drug target with auranofin as the inhibitor.
